case_number: Civil Appeal No. of 2022 (Arising out of SLP(C) No.16161 of 2018)
summary: Dispute between promotees and direct recruits over inter-se seniority for posts of Income Tax Inspectors in Gujarat. Key issues: applicability of rotation of quota principle, seniority of direct recruits whose vacancies arose in 2009-10 but were filled via CGLE-2010. The High Court had restored the 2016 seniority list, which interspaced direct recruits with 2009 promotees. Appellants (promotees) challenged this, arguing that per K. Meghachandra Singh, seniority must be from date of appointment, not vacancy year. Respondents relied on N.R. Parmar allowing earlier seniority if requisition and advertisement were in the same year. Court examined whether conditions in N.R. Parmar were met, and if its overruling in K. Meghachandra applied prospectively. Issue: whether direct recruits of 2009-10 could be placed among 2009 promotees despite appointment in 2011.
legal_provisions_cited: Article 226 of the Constitution of India
Office Memoranda dated 7th February 1986, 3rd July 1986, 22nd November 1959
Union of India v. N.R. Parmar
K. Meghachandra Singh v. Ningam Siro
final_judgment: To be disposed of on merits after considering the prospective application of K. Meghachandra Singh and factual fulfillment of N.R. Parmar conditions; status quo as of 13th July 2018 maintained.
